attendance.title: How attendance is recorded
attendance.1: Each class lists the batch's students as Present, Absent, Late or Excused. The column on the right says where each mark came from.
attendance.2: Live classes mark it automatically: a student who stays long enough in the room (LiveKit, or Teams' attendance report) is Present.
attendance.3: In a lab or classroom, show the check-in code: students type it in the live session or on the check-in page.
attendance.4: You can change any mark with a reason (for example “network dropped in the lab”). The change and the reason are kept.
attendance.5: Each night attendance feeds the readiness score (Excused is left out) and the at-risk checks; parents see their child's attendance.

interview_scoring.title: How mock interview scoring works
interview_scoring.1: Open slots for your batches; students book them on their calendar. A booked interview appears under “To score” once its time has passed.
interview_scoring.2: Score every rubric line (1 to its maximum). The college sets the rubric; the overall is the average.
interview_scoring.3: Add notes at time stamps (for example 12:40 “explained the trade-off well”) and write feedback; Tamil feedback is optional.
interview_scoring.4: Submitting is final: the student is told and sees the scores, notes and feedback. The scores feed the Communication and Track skills.
interview_scoring.5: You can attach the recording; the student plays it through a link that expires. You can delete a recording later.

code_review.title: How code review works
code_review.1: Student teams push to their GitHub repository. Each pull request comes here and is linked to its Sprint Board card.
code_review.2: Open a pull request to see the changed files, the build result and the AI reviewer's notes (patterns, complexity, risky code).
code_review.3: Comment on a line, then Approve or Request changes.
code_review.4: Approve moves the card to Done; Request changes sends it back to In progress and tells the author. A card cannot reach Done without an approved pull request.

at_risk.title: How at-risk flags work
at_risk.1: Every night the readiness run checks each student: low attendance, a falling score, missed tests and similar. A match raises a flag here.
at_risk.2: Notify parent sends the parent an in-app message, plus SMS or email, and posts in your parent thread. During quiet hours it waits until morning.
at_risk.3: Log a phone call when you actually call: record the outcome so the next person knows.
at_risk.4: Assign a mentor: the mentor and the student are told, and the mentor sees the student under My mentees.
at_risk.5: Resolve with a note when the student is back on track. Every action is kept in the flag's history.

moderation.title: How message moderation works
moderation.1: Every chat message is checked before it is saved.
moderation.2: Blocked (never posted): abusive words, phone numbers and email addresses (no private contact between students), invite links to WhatsApp or Telegram, and the college's own block words.
moderation.3: Flagged (posted, then queued here): the college's own flag words. Students can also report any message.
moderation.4: In the queue, Keep the message or Remove it with a reason; you can also mute a student in the group for a while.
moderation.5: Who can message whom is fixed by the portal: there is no private chat between students.

branch_batch.title: How branches and batches work
branch_batch.1: A branch is a department, for example CSE or AI & DS. It has a code, a track and an optional HoD.
branch_batch.2: A batch is a class group inside a branch for one semester and academic year, for example “AI&DS Sem 5 A”.
branch_batch.3: Students are imported into a batch, and trainers are mapped to batches: a trainer sees only their batches.
branch_batch.4: Promote moves a batch to the next semester. Readiness and reports drill down by branch, then batch, then student.

readiness.title: How placement readiness works
readiness.1: It is the same score the student sees on their dashboard, recomputed every night from attendance, tests, coding, interviews and projects.
readiness.2: You see aggregates: band counts and the average per branch and batch, this month's trend, and the weakest skill per batch.
readiness.3: Drill down to a student to see their score and band.
readiness.4: Trainer notes and chats are never shown here.

drives.title: How mock drives work
drives.1: A drive simulates a company's hiring process. Create a “drive” event on Events, then set the company pattern here.
drives.2: Add rounds: a test round (a published test with a cut-off %) or an interview round (trainer, time, slots, cut-off score).
drives.3: Publishing turns interview rounds into slots on the trainer's Mock interviews screen; students book them as usual.
drives.4: Results show each student's round scores and cut-offs. Students who clear every round are shortlisted; publishing the shortlist tells them and freezes the results.

timetable.title: Who changes the timetable
timetable.1: Trainers don't edit the timetable directly. From their Schedule they propose a new session, a reschedule, a cancellation or a substitute.
timetable.2: A college admin approves or rejects each request here. Clashes with rooms or other classes are warned about.
timetable.3: On approval the trainer and the batch's students are told, and the session appears on their calendars.
timetable.4: A placement officer can view the timetable but not change it.
